      Problem: Lines: 3765-3784 (Telegram editor-changes-lost warning step) and 3710 (where CHANGES_LOST_REDISPATCHED is set to "skipped_peer_inflight"); Code reference:; Line 3710 (editor_changes_lost_retrigger):; echo "CHANGES_LOST_REDISPATCHED=skipped_peer_inflight" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"; Line 3765 (Telegram warning):; if [ "${CHANGES_LOST_REDISPATCHED:-false}" = "true" ]; then; ... (retrying message); if [ "${CAN_PUSH:-}" = "true" ]; then; ... (exhausted message)  <-- This fires incorrectly; The conditional at 3765 only matches CHANGES_LOST_REDISPATCHED="true". When the retrigger is correctly skipped because a peer run is already in flight, the step sets CHANGES_LOST_REDISPATCHED="skipped_peer_inflight" (line 3710). That value falls through to the else branch which emits a misleading CRITICAL "Editor changes lost (exhausted)" message (and posts a PR comment stating "All retries exhausted"), even though the workflow behaved correctly and no retry was needed.; Admins see a false alarm notification implying the autofix cycle failed, when in fact the deduplication logic successfully avoided a redundant dispatch. This erodes trust in telemetry and wastes time investigating a non-issue.; --- ISSUE 2: Peer detection does not filter by PR number, causing false positives when multiple PRs share the same head branch ===

  [6] File: scripts/gh_helpers.sh (line ~1102)
      Problem: Lines: 1133-1142 (jq filter inside autofix_retrigger_has_inflight_peer, function defined at 1102); Code reference:; peer_info=$(printf '%s' "${response}" | jq -r --arg current "${current_run_id}" '; .workflow_runs[]?; | select(.status == "queued" or .status == "in_progress"); | select((.id | tostring) != $current); | select(.path | test("(^|/)(review_autofix|internal-review|ai-review)\\.ya?ml$")); | {count: length, first_id: (.[0].id // "-"), first_path: (.[0].path // "-")}; | "\(.count) \(.first_id) \(.first_path)"; ' 2>/dev/null || echo "0 - -"); The jq filter correctly excludes the current run ID and matches workflow path, but does NOT verify that a candidate peer run is associated with the same PR number. The function receives PR number as $1 (pr_number) but never passes it to jq. In repos where feature branches are shared across PRs (common in trunk-based workflows where a long-lived feature branch is updated across several PR revisions), a peer run from a different PR on the same branch will be treated as a match and cause the retrigger to skip unnecessarily. The skipped PR then fails to schedule a new review iteration and may stall.; PR A's retrigger observes PR B's in-flight review run on the same head branch and incorrectly skips its own dispatch. PR A never gets a fresh review pass and may remain stuck while PR B is being processed separately.; --- ISSUE 3: Branch filtering ambiguity may cause false positives when base/head branch names overlap ===

      Problem: The GitHub Actions API `branch` filter is ambiguous; it returns runs for the specified branch name regardless of whether it is a head branch or a base branch. It also does not distinguish between a branch in the upstream repo and a branch with the same name in a fork.; If a PR is opened from a fork's `main` branch, the helper might detect unrelated `review_autofix` runs on the upstream `main` branch as peers, incorrectly skipping a necessary retrigger for the PR.; HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS:

      Problem: Line/code reference: Lines 1121-1132 in `autofix_retrigger_has_inflight_peer` function; The GitHub Actions API endpoint `/repos/{repo}/actions/runs?branch={branch}` filters by branch name but does not differentiate between a base branch and a head branch in cross-repository PRs when both have the same name. For example, if a PR is opened from a fork with head branch "main" targeting upstream "main", any review workflow run on the upstream main branch would be incorrectly treated as a peer.; A PR from a fork with head branch "main" could have its retrigger incorrectly skipped if there is an active review workflow on the upstream "main" branch. The `head_branch` in a PR context from a fork is the name of the branch in the fork, which could collide with base branch names.; **Issue 3: PR number not verified in peer detection filter**

  [13] File: scripts/gh_helpers.sh
      Problem: Lines: 1113-1115 (API call) and 1133-1142 (jq filter); Code reference:; API request (line 1115):; "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs?branch=${head_branch}&per_page=30"; The GitHub Actions List runs API's `branch` parameter will match both base and head runs when the repository has an ongoing workflow run on a branch having the same name as the PR's head branch. For example, if a fork contributor opens a PR with head branch "main", upstream's own "main" branch runs will appear in the response. Since the filter doesn't narrow by `.head_branch` to confirm the run actually belongs to the PR head, such unrelated runs can be misidentified as peers if they match the workflow path and status criteria.; A retrigger for a fork PR whose head branch is "main" could be skipped because a review run on upstream "main" is in flight.
